title: Synthesis and Properties of Erbium Isopropoxides: Structural Characterization of Er5O(OPri)13

material_class.structural_family: solvated non-oxo erbium isopropoxide (structure not determined)

synthesis.procedure: Route 2A (preferred high-yield metathesis without added water): potassium (12.79 mmol, 0.500 g) was dissolved in 20 mL of a 1:1 (vol:vol) 2-propanol–toluene mixture, then anhydrous ErCl3 (4.263 mmol, 1.176 g) was added. After 2 days at room temperature the mixture was centrifuged to remove the white precipitate; the solution was gently evaporated almost to dryness and a small amount of 2-propanol was added, giving pink I essentially free of K and Cl by SEM–EDS (yield 90–95%). Route 2B is the same procedure at 75 °C with equal yield. Route 1: Er metal chips (11.96 mmol, 2.000 g) in 40 mL of 1:1 toluene/HOPri with ca. 1 mg HgCl2 catalyst were heated at 75 °C for 24–48 h; centrifugation gave an olive precipitate and a reddish-pink solution that was gently evaporated to a pink sticky mass of I (yield 40–45%). All preparations were handled under dry oxygen-free argon (glove box); heated reactions used closed vessels under P2O5-dried nitrogen.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: glove box (dry Ar); closed vessels under dry N2 for heated reactions; centrifugation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: centrifuge off white (or olive) precipitate; gently evaporate the pink solution almost to dryness and add a small amount of 2-propanol (route 2); gentle evaporation of the reddish-pink solution to a pink sticky mass (route 1)

properties.summary: UV–vis spectrum of I in 2-propanol (190–900 nm) shows typical Er3+ bands; the fine structure of the 2H11/2 ← 4I15/2 transition (and 4G11/2 and 4F9/2 ← 4I15/2) was used for identification. Crystal/solution color is reddish pink. No magnetic data reported.

measurements.name: UV–vis absorption (Er3+ f–f bands)
measurements.value: typical Er3+ bands; 2H11/2 ← 4I15/2 fine structure used for identification (Fig. 2)

synthesis.procedure: Preferred direct route 3 (metathesis with hydrolysis): K (11.0 mmol, 0.429 g) was dissolved in 16 mL of 1:1 (vol:vol) 2-propanol–toluene, followed by dropwise addition of 0.73 mL of 1 M H2O (0.73 mmol) in 2-propanol–toluene 2:1. After 1 h, ErCl3 (3.655 mmol, 1.000 g) was added and allowed to react 2 days at room temperature; centrifugation removed a white precipitate. Evaporation of the solution gave crystals identified by IR as pure Er5O(OPri)13, free of K and Cl by SEM–EDS. Alternative: thorough evaporation of I and recrystallization from toluene gave Er5O(OPri)13 in close to quantitative yield from I. Hydrolysis of I in 2-propanol by slow addition of 1 M H2O in toluene–2-propanol (2:1) at Er:H2O = 5:1 also produced Er5O(OPri)13 in almost stoichiometric yield. Preparations under dry oxygen-free argon.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature (route 3); recrystallization from I after thorough evaporation
synthesis.time: 1 h after water addition then 2 days after ErCl3 addition (route 3)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: glove box (dry Ar); centrifugation; closed vessels for heated reactions
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: centrifuge off white precipitate; evaporate solvent from the solution to give crystals (easier than routes 1–2). From I: thorough evaporation and recrystallization from toluene.
synthesis.yield: high-yield formation by route 3 (exact % not stated); close to quantitative from I; almost stoichiometric from hydrolysis of I at Er:H2O = 5:1

properties.summary: UV–vis spectra of Er5O(OPri)13 show typical Er3+ f–f transitions; the fine structure of the 2H11/2 ← 4I15/2 band in toluene–2-propanol (2:1) was used for identification and to follow conversion to ErAl3(OPri)12. Reddish-pink crystals. No magnetic data reported.

measurements.value: Er3+ f–f fine structure used for identification (Fig. 4)
